audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Trundle five of seven stages while five of the seven why-texts underneath describe Sylas winning — whys[1] 'turning your power island into his fight zone', whys[2] 'he wins the full skirmish', whys[4] 'you hand him the best version of your own ultimate', whys[5], and whys[6] 'the 1v1 belongs to him'. Level 1 was scored for Trundle while spikes[3] and whys[0] both call it neutral.
audit.why: 513 games, the largest sample in the slice, at 49.51% — a coin flip. The duel itself is Sylas-favoured after level 2 and the text has always said so; the near-even win rate comes from Trundle's objective and teamfight value, not from beating Sylas in a side lane.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Sylas / Sylas / Skill / Sylas / Sylas / Sylas in both layers, matching the packet's stage read and all seven why-texts. The 2+ items why now states explicitly that the lane loss and the even win rate are not a contradiction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike never gives Hijack's cooldown, so it reads as an occasional threat.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30s and Subjugate is 120/100/80s. He gets your ultimate on a shorter cooldown than you do, at every rank — by rank 3 it is 30 seconds against your 80. That is the fact that makes 'never R first' correct rather than cautious.
audit.corrected: Hijack's 80/55/30s cooldown and 950 steal range written into spikes[1], whys[4], mid and breakdown.cooldowns, against Subjugate's 120/100/80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names no Sylas ability (packet defect) and gets three mechanics wrong. (a) 'his W drain heal ticks on you continuously' — Kingslayer is a single lunge that damages and heals on champion hit, 12s at rank 1 falling to 6s at rank 5, not a channelled drain. (b) breakdown.cooldowns calls Abscond/Abduct 'his dash + stun (recast pull)'; there is no stun — it is a dash, and the recast throws chains to pull HIM to an enemy hit. (c) Chomp is called an AS-steal twice; it saps attack damage.
audit.why: Whether Kingslayer is a burst heal or a channel decides the entire trade plan — a burst heal on a 12-second cooldown is a window you can wait out, a channel is not.
audit.corrected: Chain Lash, Kingslayer, Abscond/Abduct, Hijack and Petricite Burst all named with cooldowns; Kingslayer described as a lunge with a heal on champion hit; the phantom stun removed; the sap corrected to attack damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says 'Respect the E cooldown window — it is roughly 14 seconds at rank 1'. Abscond/Abduct is 13/12/11/10/9s.
audit.why: The whole early plan is 'trade only while E is burned'. Being told the window is 14 seconds when it is 13 means the player is standing next to a Sylas who already has his dash back.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 13s at rank 1 and carried into whys[1], whys[3], mid and breakdown.cooldowns, with Kingslayer's 12s rank-1 cooldown added as the second thing to count.

audit.whatIsWrong: Kingslayer's heal is discussed in four fields and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned once.
audit.why: Riot's Kingslayer text heals him against enemy champions, and the missing-interactions file flags this exact matchup for anti-heal. Trundle's own answer to the lane is a Frozen Domain that amplifies healing, so a healing race he loses is precisely the race the matchup describes him entering.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into wants.you[2], whys[5] and late, tied to his first AP item rather than as a generic buy.

edits.after: Abscond (13s at rank 1) comes online and the recast pulls him back onto you to land Kingslayer's heal — off Frozen Domain, he wins the long fight.

edits.after: Hijack is 80s at rank 1 against Subjugate's 120s — he steals your ultimate and gets it back sooner than you do, so never open with R unless it kills.

edits.after: His first AP item turns Kingslayer's champion heal into a real loop — buy Grievous Wounds here or long trades stop paying.

edits.after: Chomp's attack-damage sap and King's Tribute healing off dying minions make the first trade neutral — neither side wants a long brawl yet.

edits.after: Hijack Subjugate at level 6 and second-cast it to pull your armor and MR back onto himself

edits.after: Out-sustain you with Kingslayer's champion heal, then kill you on the cooldown window you opened

edits.after: Chomp's attack-damage sap makes the opener neutral — neither of you has the sustained damage to secure a kill, so farm and respect his range.

edits.after: Abscond arrives at level 2 on a 13-second rank-1 cooldown, and the recast chains him back to you — he decides where the fight happens, not your Frozen Domain.

edits.before: Both kits are active but neither spike has landed; trade on his E cooldown window and use Pillar to trap him, keeping this stage skill-dependent.
edits.after: Both kits are active but no spike has landed; trade in the 13 seconds after Abscond is spent and use Pillar of Ice to hold him, and this stage stays a read.

edits.before: Sylas steals Subjugate and his second cast drains the armor and MR you just stole — you hand him the best version of your own ultimate every time you R.
edits.after: Hijack is 80s at rank 1 against your 120s Subjugate, so he casts your ultimate more often than you do — every R you open with is one he gets to answer with.

edits.before: His AP mythic makes W healing outrageously efficient; Chomp's regen cannot keep pace with the burst-heal loop he runs in every drawn-out trade.
edits.after: His AP item makes Kingslayer's champion heal efficient enough that Chomp's regen cannot keep pace — Grievous Wounds keeps this stage playable.

edits.before: Full AP Sylas at two items out-bursts your resistance stack and E-dashes out of Frozen Domain before your regen matters — the 1v1 belongs to him.
edits.after: Two items in, the duel belongs to him: he bursts through your resists and Abscond leaves your zone. Your 49.51% comes from objectives, not this island.

edits.before: At level 1 neither of you has a real kill threat — Q Chomp the first minion wave trade, heal the chip from his Q through passive, and accept that it is roughly neutral. The danger starts at level 2: the moment Sylas picks up E he can dash through your Pillar or dodge into Frozen Domain where HE benefits from the fight going long, because his W drain heal ticks on you continuously. Respect the E cooldown window — it is roughly 14 seconds at rank 1 — and only trade aggressively while it is burned.
edits.after: At level 1 neither of you has a real kill threat — Chomp the first wave trade, heal his chip back through King's Tribute, and accept a neutral opener. The danger starts at level 2: Abscond is a dash on a 13-second rank-1 cooldown, and the recast throws chains that pull HIM to whatever they hit, so he re-enters the fight on his own terms and lands Kingslayer's champion heal. That heal is a single lunge every 12 seconds at rank 1, not a channel, so it is a window you can wait out. Trade aggressively only while both are spent.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the only neutral window in this lane and you need to use them carefully. Sylas is ahead on kill pressure but not yet at his full AP spike; drop Frozen Domain early to bait his E, then re-place it behind him once he has committed the dash so he cannot kite out. Your Pillar cutting off his exit is the single most important mechanical play in this matchup — a Sylas who cannot dash away dies inside W. At level 6 the dynamic flips hard: he steals Subjugate and can drain your armor and MR while you are trying to drain his, effectively doubling the ultimate's value for himself. Do not R into him unless you have enough burst to kill before the steal lands its second cast.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the only neutral window in this lane and you need to use them carefully. Sylas is ahead on kill pressure but not at his AP spike yet; drop Frozen Domain early to bait Abscond, then re-place it behind him once the dash is committed. Pillar of Ice on his exit is the single most important mechanical play here — a Sylas who cannot reposition dies inside your W, and the dash is 13 seconds at rank 1. At level 6 the dynamic flips hard: Hijack has 950 range and an 80-second cooldown at rank 1, against Subjugate's 120, so he steals your ultimate and gets it back before you do. Do not cast R into him unless the burst behind it kills before his second cast lands.

edits.before: By first item Sylas's AP mythic makes his W heal disproportionate to the damage you deal per trade, and he outpaces your resistance regen with raw burst. Your Iceborn Gauntlet shred and Chomp AS-steal still make you a credible side-laner, but the 1v1 is no longer favorable. Shift your value to objective fights where Subjugate on their front-line tank still drains real stats, accept that Sylas owns the top-lane island, and look for flanks onto his backline rather than matching him directly.
edits.after: By first item Sylas's AP mythic makes Kingslayer's champion heal disproportionate to what you deal per trade, and Grievous Wounds is what keeps you in the race. Your Iceborn Gauntlet and Chomp's attack-damage sap still make you a credible side-laner, but the 1v1 is no longer favourable. Shift your value to objective fights, where Subjugate on their front-line tank drains real stats rather than a squishy's, accept that Sylas owns the top-lane island, and look for flanks onto his backline instead of matching him.

edits.after: Two items in he wins the island: he bursts through your resists, then Abscond leaves your zone. Your value moves to objectives and 5v5s instead.

notes: Unverified and therefore not written: whether Abscond dashes THROUGH Pillar of Ice's terrain. The existing text asserts 'he can dash through your Pillar' in two places; Riot's text says only 'Sylas dashes to a location', so I rewrote those clauses around what is verifiable (the 13-second rank-1 cooldown and the recast pull) rather than restating or denying the terrain claim. Judgement call for the user: I gave Sylas five of seven stages in a 49.51% matchup. The prose has always described a losing duel, and 49.51 over 513 games is a coin flip that Trundle's map value can explain — but if the user prefers the chart to track the headline win rate rather than the lane, levels 4-5 or 2+ items are the stages to move back.
